first.rationale: Two pressures (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same funnel stage, and the competitor's pricing move is the loudest but not necessarily the highest-value lever. Under the triage invariant I verify the beliefs that are both decision-critical and weakest against the stated objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue). memory_86 is the direct warrant for my intended action, but its recorded outcomes are proxies — completion rate and time-to-value — with no evidence they translated into retained, qualified revenue; if the original record shows only funnel-stage lift, the case for acting on it weakens sharply. memory_73 is the strongest competing pull given the competitor launch, and it is the single riskiest inherited belief here: 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' says nothing about margin, retention, or the quality of accounts acquired on discount, and price cuts are hard to reverse once a segment anchors on them. Verifying it protects against spending the only slot this week on revenue that decays. I deliberately do not verify memory_31 despite its relevance — it overlaps with memory_86 on the same mechanism, so the marginal information is low; I note, though, that cutting required signup fields is exactly the kind of change that can lift activation counts while degrading lead qualification downstream, so any onboarding test must instrument qualified-revenue and retention guardrails, not just completion. memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) and memory_57 (referrals) are plausible but neither addresses the acute quarter-over-quarter declines, so they are not decision-critical this week. I keep the scale to a small guarded test: the inherited evidence supports the direction but not yet the magnitude or the durability, and committing broadly on proxy-metric evidence would convert an unverified belief into an organizational fact. If the archive shows memory_86 was measured on retained revenue rather than completion alone, I would escalate to a standard experiment; if it shows proxies only, I hold at guarded scale and treat the result as provisional.

final.rationale: Both verifications paid off, and in opposite directions. exp_73 is now a clear disqualification, not a caution: the 40% targeted discount bought +31% signup and +18% qualified revenue while destroying 30-day retention (-12%), and the original record explicitly concluded the cohort does not survive first renewal and that discounting should NOT be generalized as sustainable growth. That warning was stripped out when memory_73 was consolidated into 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' — exactly the failure mode the triage invariant exists to catch. Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, responding to the competitor's entry pricing with promotional_pricing would be optimizing the metric the source record already showed to be misleading. I am also recording that the inherited summary is wrong and should be corrected, not just ignored this week. exp_86 held up on the dimension I doubted: the lift was not proxy-only — 30-day retention +3% alongside completion +13% and time-to-value -2.1 days. That converts my guarded posture into a justified standard experiment, and it addresses both acute declines at once, since onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%) share this funnel stage. I still preserve uncertainty on two points. First, exp_86 measured retention at 30 days, whereas exp_73's damage only became visible at the renewal cycle; a 30-day positive does not by itself establish durability, so this test must be instrumented to renewal, not just to completion. Second, memory_31's mechanism — cutting required signup fields — can inflate activation counts while degrading lead qualification, so I will hold field reduction out of scope or gate it behind qualified-revenue guardrails rather than bundling it in. I decline broad_rollout: the evidence supports the direction and now supports meaningful scale, but not a company-wide commitment on a single archived result. The competitor pressure is real and unaddressed by this choice; the honest answer is that the verified-sustainable lever and the fast-relief lever are different levers, and I am spending the one slot on the former.
